The ending feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned. The central conflict of the story—the missing waterproof membrane and the ensuing months of disruptive, bureaucratic chaos—reaches its logical conclusion when the repairs are finally finished and it rains without the ceiling leaking ("Miriam watched the ceiling. Nothing happened."). Furthermore, secondary plot threads, such as Noor's precarious working conditions, are resolved through her securing a new job in Glasgow. The final image of Miriam hesitating to move the empty bucket and ultimately walking around it serves as a resonant, thematic callback to her earlier joke ("THIS BUCKET IS IN USE"), subtly illustrating the lingering caution and institutional fatigue left behind by the ordeal.
